subject.title: Feature Request: Add parseMode config for Telegram channels

question: Should Telegram expose a public parse/text-mode config, and which modes plus override levels should be supported?
rationale: The missing source surface is clear, but adding it changes Telegram's documented delivery, escaping, compatibility, and security contract, so automation should not choose the product shape.

options.title: Add a narrow text-mode config
options.body: Support a conservative top-level and per-account mode such as `plain` versus current HTML-safe rendering, leaving MarkdownV2/raw HTML/custom entities for separate design.

options.title: Keep existing knobs only
options.body: Treat `richMessages` and `markdown.tables` as the supported formatting controls and close or narrow this request after maintainer confirmation.

options.title: Design full parse-mode support
options.body: Sponsor a broader Telegram contract for HTML, MarkdownV2, custom emojis/entities, escaping, fallback behavior, and live proof expectations.

recommendation.title: Add a narrow text-mode config
recommendation.body: Support a conservative top-level and per-account mode such as `plain` versus current HTML-safe rendering, leaving MarkdownV2/raw HTML/custom entities for separate design.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter introduced the current HTML formatting baseline and has the strongest local history across Telegram formatting, config, and docs.
